mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp in 1 month, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS declines for 2 consecutive months, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to increased corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases > 1% MoM, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same period, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and UNRATE increases > 0.3pp
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST declines > 10% YoY and UNRATE increases > 0.3pp, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5 percentage points in a quarter, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5pp in a quarter, or if the Rank IC of this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
